data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The workspace must be treated as a causal broadcast medium emitting content-hash pings into an external Merkle DAG, making reclamation a data-availability query rather than a liveness check, since a crashed process cannot self-witness its own death.","counterconditions":[{"case":"All witness agents fail simultaneously with the process","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The DAG suffers an eclipse attack or partition that hides evidence","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Byzantine witnesses equivocate on the Merkle root","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Network latency makes DAG witness visibility slower than reclamation timeout, reintroducing the race condition","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Drawing from the broadcast-medium inversion: every write to the workspace emits a content-hash 'ping' into a durable Merkle DAG before the write is acknowledged. Reclamation asks not 'is the process alive?' but 'has any node ever witnessed the final evidence state for this problem ID?' The durable record must contain: (1) the Merkle root of witnessed hashes, (2) the problem-workspace binding as a DAG node, and (3) a witness quorum attestation. This directly addresses the crash-without-terminal-record by removing the process from the critical path of safety; the process merely proposes evidence, and the DAG confirms it.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
